text: The subject, Bilal Ali (PK**UNIL****5275), a freelance software developer with a declared monthly income of PKR 90,000, received a series of high‑value inbound IBFT transfers from ten different counterparties between 2 Mar and 11 Mar 2026. In the 14‑day window the inbound amounts total PKR 560,000, with each individual credit ranging from PKR 34,000 to PKR 89,000 and originating from multiple synthetic banks and distinct individuals (e.g., Zeeshan Yousaf, Faisal Farooq, Mehwish Tariq). The typology engine flagged this pattern (score 360) for “many distinct inbound counterparties” and “large share of inbound value leaves quickly.” Within hours of the last inbound credit, on 13 Mar 2026 the account made a single outbound transaction of PKR 159,000 via an ATM withdrawal and, more notably, an out‑of‑account wallet transfer of PKR 235,000 to a QuickPay e‑wallet (WLT****0932). The rapid conversion of aggregated inbound funds into cash and a wallet transfer, without any apparent business justification, is characteristic of a “border mule” scheme used to move illicit proceeds. Given the volume, speed, and structure of the transactions, a Suspicious Transaction Report is warranted.
